I can only apologise for the erratic explanations of my way of thinking. It goes against everything I'm trying to do, but untill I've put it all together in the correct order in my head I'm going to struggle to write it down in a logical order.

It essentially comes down to the following sentence;

Look for a decision that goes against the previous market perceptions of value, it should be a point in the chart where it could either keeping going in the same direction as the previous tend or make a decision to go the other way. It should be a big decision, strong imbalance that not only goes against the previous minor trend but also makes an effort to set underway a bigger change. A decision to engulf a significant high.

Momentum before and after the decision are prefered but I believe it is not always necessary to have it before. If we FTR to our decision then watch for a fakeout. I'll give some examples of this later. Of to the hospital for the rest of the day now.

Stay safe everyone.

text:
Well I can let you all know that it clearly hasn't.

I'm trawling thr site, almost every significant post and what I can say is their is not much consistency on the reasons for taking trades.

The definition of the FL, which i struggle to find in the flag limit article is so ambiguous it's unreal. I have charts from master traders where they have marked FL's in many different ways, some say it's the decision to engulf yet they mark a decision that has already engulfed i.e. price prices a high/S/R oir another FL and retraces then carries on in the same direction.

Unless I'm being totally stupid, a decision to engulf has to be made before the engulf. So, which is it? I would really appreciate some feedback?

Take this chart and comments by harry, he has the Fl as the FTR AFTER the engulf. If it turns price then that's fair enough, but here harry says it's because of the imbalance of left over orders, but surely the real imbalance is in the green box under the S/R, where the imbalance was so great it pushed price through the S/R, surely this is the point where buyers really show their hand, especially as it is the edge of CP.

It's seem like commons sense that an FTR is reacting of an important decision, If it does not reach the decision we think is important do we deem the FTR unreliable because of possible fakeouts? Or do we say that demand/supply was so high that we are confident we should take a trade there anyway?

In my mind, the last line of defense of a FLAG has to be the decision to leave it as this must be where the orders are left? an FTR must always secondary, I can't see how Harrys FL is anything but an FTR.

Unless there is something to the left? We're always told to look left to see what the highs are reacting off yet all of the instructional posts are using a recent high or low?

I think clarity would help us all, I'm sure someone will say it has been said before, and you're right, it has, but it seems the right hand is doing one thing and the left hand is doing another. either their is a set way of marking FL's or it is just pure luck. The only thing I can currently see working is following decisions around the chart. Everything else seems like gambling.

Can anyone of any authority clarify this? Is a FLAG limit a Decision to engulf?

author: Whenever
text:
Hi Robbie,

even not being an expert too, I would like to give all the possible support as well, as I think we are all rowing in the same direction. I may be of course wrong, so we can discuss our opinions.

First of all my thought about FLs: they ARE a decision.

But not to Engulf. They are a decision that an EG is a real EG and not a FO! Therefore important.

Let's think about a rally: Price EG the last Supply level (SR or Supply) and searches for the next higher Balance (it is all a matter of Lots in both directions). As soon as it finds it, it stops (that's the balance). Then Supply takes over again, using all Buy Orders and looking for below further balance.

In case of a FO, there is no Demand there anymore, so it still drops.

In case of Real EG the Buy orders take over again at a certain point, and the rally starts again - Taking over all the above Supply. That's the Battle Won! That's the DP and the FTR and the end (Limit) of the F.L.

About not receiving any feedback, I think we cannot expect any Master stopping by in all the posts. But what I am trying to do is to get the only real feedback from the charts. In other words: you have a theory about reading price, look at it in some charts. If you don't get the imagined reaction, then it sounds like some Master said: "you are wrong, look at our Journals again".

Perhaps (and here I fully agree with Distinction) we all sometimes want too much. To may see any singular reason of any singular move in price. That's Greedy: one of Trading's Devils.

Or we are impatient and want to see all possible setup for not waiting any longer and TRADE!

My suggestion (and my point of this Journey too): try to Master one Set Up only. Forget about PAZ for a while, and look at SR of HTF. EG => FL => FTR => FTB.

I am of the opinion too, that mastering those we could make enough to have no need of further investigating. May be we will want. Then we will study why and when they fail, and price goes further to look for the DP to EG (the origin of Supply).

But till then I would suggest: clear your mind from TOO MUCH (I say to myself as first of course) and learn to WAIT. Psichology will be trained, Focus will be trained and with high probability Balance will grow

Sorry for the long post and do not hesitate to critic or reply: mine is not the absolute Truth Just some thoughts after some experience.

Thanks for dropping by mate, so, I'm so gland you referenced that article, so, 'price makes a decision before continuing down', this is part of my problem, I look at this article nearly everyday.

Lets take whenevers decription;

'Let's think about a rally: Price EG the last Supply level (SR or Supply) and searches for the next higher Balance (it is all a matter of Lots in both directions). As soon as it finds it, it stops (that's the balance). Then Supply takes over again, using all Buy Orders and looking for below further balance.'

That right here is my issue with FLAG limits, IV5758, do you agree with the above statement?

We all agree that a FL is a decision, it is a decision to continue in the direction of the previous momentum, which means not only is it the end of momentum but also the start of momentum, this is why it is a barrier between zones.

In the diagram below, whenevers description would mean that 'A' was the FL because 'Price rallied' 'It engulfed the previous supply level' snf the FTR'd, remember, there is no FTR without an engulf, that is clear in the FTR article. Lets reference the FL article again, the examples given, there is a clear difference, one engulfs the supply to the left and the other doesn't, does this not make you ask questions?

Example one from the FL article, price drops and clearly engulfs the low or s/r before making it's decision, it fails to return and carrys on in the direction of the previous momentum.

Example two from the FL article, price drops, it clearly doesn't engulf the low or s/r harry has marked, it makes a decision and carrys on in the direction of the previous momentum.

So, we have two clear scenarios, they're documented in the article by Harry, so which is correct? By the definition you have both suggested to me Harrys second example is not a FL, do you agree with that?

IV5758, I completely agree with this statement you made

'From my current understanding, price drops and FLAG (BASE) then drops again. FTB is where we want to trade which is the BASE/FLAG. BASE is where decision is made whether price is too cheap or expensive.'

I am not disagreeing with this, what I am seeing is that it is irrelevant whether the decision' have engulfed the high or low to it's left. This decsion can still be an FTR and a decision to engulf, for example...

Remember, it is suggested by all the masters that you look for what is holding price up or down and consider what is to the left before an engulf is valid. FL's hold price up and down. The only common factor that can be applied in both of Harrys examples is that price decided to engulf the decision holding up price, a previous FL.

If anyone can give a different explanation of why both examples are FL's I would love to hear it as this is what is sending me around in circles.

I have just opened MT4 at random and done this to prove a point. does anyone disagree that they are FL's?

(numbered just for you Rob)

Thank you all for your input, unfortunately i don't think people are quite grasping where I'm coming from with this but hopefully you might after this post
